item.title: Paraguay prosecutor will seek charges against embattled president after bank collapse
item.description:
Santiago Peña’s rightwing administration had authorised Ueno Bank to drastically expand operations before collapse Paraguay’s rightwing president, Santiago Peña, resigned on Thursday after a political and financial crisis collapsed the South American country’s banking system in recent days. At the centre of the crisis is Ueno Bank, which in just a few years under Peña went from an obscure digital bank to one of the country’s largest lenders, claiming to have about 60% of Paraguay’s adult population as customers. item.title: Hoax bomb threats force emergency landings, evacuations across Europe
item.description:
Planes forced into emergency landings or diversions two days after hoax alerts affected air travel Why have more than 30 European flights been hit by bomb threats this week? Hoax bomb threats have caused at least 34 flights across Europe to be disrupted, with some forced to make emergency landings, as questions mount over an apparently coordinated effort to cause chaos for travellers. The series of warnings on Thursday affected flights between Italy, Ireland, the UK, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, France, Greece, Serbia and Czechia. item.title: Trump met Russian envoy after he appeared with Melania Trump and Ukrainians
item.description:
Photo Illustration by Thomas Levinson/The Daily Beast/Reuters Melania Trump praised the Russians; she praised the Ukrainians; she touted her senior adviser; but she didn’t mention her husband, Donald Trump, at her event on Thursday. The first lady held the gathering at the White House to celebrate the temporary ceasefire deal in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, which concluded on November 1. It came as the president has come up short on his own promise to bring about an end to the war in Ukraine, which has been raging since Russia invaded in 2022. He previously claimed he could end the war on day one of his second term. Read more at The Daily Beast.

item.title: Melania Trump touts rare agreement she brokered between Russia and Ukraine
item.description:
As war rages on in Kyiv and other cities, the first lady celebrates her single-city ceasefire with Russian and Ukrainian envoys Beaming from a podium in the White House’s Grand Foyer, Melania Trump welcomed senior Russian and Ukrainian officials on Thursday to celebrate a ceasefire in an embattled Ukrainian town for which she has become the unlikeliest broker. The evacuation from Oleshky, a frontline Ukrainian town now occupied by Russia where 800 people lived through a protracted humanitarian crisis, may seem like a sideshow at this point in the war. Russian missiles and drones continue to rain down on Kyiv and other major cities, and a single Russian strike described as a “double-tap” bombing killed 40 people in Zaporizhzhia on Wednesday. item.title: Arab party backs Eisenkot in bid to form Israel’s next government
item.description:
President says he will make a decision on Sunday about who should try to build a government as Netanyahu rival is endorsed by 67 lawmakers Gadi Eisenkot, the main rival to Benjamin Netanyahu, secured endorsements on Thursday from a majority of lawmakers to try to form a government but Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, said it was still unclear who could break the deadlock and that he would decide on Sunday which of the two men should try first. Of the Knesset’s 120 elected lawmakers, 67 had endorsed Eisenkot through several days of talks with Herzog, while 46 endorsed Netanyahu. Herzog said on Thursday that while the “results ‌of the consultations may appear clear”, there were “mutual vetoes between the blocs and within the blocs themselves” that make it difficult to say who has the ‌best shot to form a government. Continue reading...

item.title: Alabama executes man for 1991 killings in last of 3 U.S. executions carried out the same day
item.description:
Unusual instance of three states administering the death penalty on the same day previously happened in 2010 Alabama, Florida and Indiana all carried out executions on Thursday in an unusual instance of three states administering the death penalty on the same day. In a record-tying 19th execution of the year, Florida executed Jesse Guardado via a three-drug lethal injection. Guardado had pleaded guilty to fatally stabbing a 75-year-old woman inside her Walton county home in 2004 before stealing her jewelry box, $80 and other valuables to buy drugs. The woman had helped him get a job and housing. Continue reading...

item.title: Gina Hinojosa won the governor’s race. What happens to Texas data centers now?
item.description:
AUSTIN, Texas — Gina Hinojosa is set to become the next governor of Texas after voters denied Republican Gov. Greg Abbott a fourth term, a stunning upset by a state legislator who will become the first Latina to hold the Lone Star State’s top job. Hinojosa mounted a competitive bid against Abbott with a disciplined focus on corruption, which she argued is to blame for soaring prices, declining public schools and the aggressive expansion of data centers. Hinojosa capitalized on the financial strain that pushed voters who had supported President Donald Trump to grow disillusioned with the Republican Party. “It bothered me that they doubted us,” Hinojosa told a crowd of supporters at an election night event in Austin to uproar. “Now I stand before you humbled and grateful.” Hinojosa will be the first Texas governor from the Rio Grande Valley, a heavily Latino part of the state, and the…

item.title: Anti-Trans Panic Couldn’t Save Republicans in Deep-Red Texas
item.description:
On an election night handing Republicans a beating in critical House and Senate races across the country, the GOP fell short even in once deep-red Texas after a campaign run on a go-to outrage tactic: fearmongering over the rights of transgender people. Democrats escaped the political wilderness in the Longhorn State on Tuesday night, when Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton — despite the far-right attorney general’s relentless attacks on the trans community and his party’s claims that Democrats would enforce so-called “transgenderism” as a kind of ideology. item.title: Democrats promised to end corruption. Here’s how they can do that | David Sirota
item.description:
Now that Democrats have secured earth-shattering wins in both chambers of Congress, the party’s progressives are sending a message to their more moderate leaders: It’s time to deliver for voters who are demanding meaningful action. “Even where the candidate wasn’t a self-described progressive, progressives won big last night,” said Congressional Progressive Caucus Chair Greg Casar, D-Texas, during a press call on Wednesday. “Across the country, so-called moderate candidates ran on ending forever wars,” he added, pointing out that Democrats went after the GOP for voting down congressional attempts to stop President Donald Trump’s unpopular military actions — efforts that the progressive caucus had organized.
